title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Evaluation of calf pain while walking.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old woman presenting for a follow-up regarding symptoms of claudication. She reports significant calf pain that occurs specifically during long walks but resolves quickly with rest. She denies any pain while at rest. She notes that the discomfort is localized exclusively to her right leg. She denies any skin breakdown or changes in sensation.

Medication List
Atorvastatin 40mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Aspirin 81mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and in no acute distress. Physical examination of the right lower extremity reveals diminished pedal pulses compared to the unaffected side. The skin is intact with no signs of breakdown. Capillary refill is less than 3 seconds.

Assessment
The patient has atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. This is manifesting as intermittent claudication involving the right leg only.

Plan
Continue current antiplatelet and lipid-lowering medications. The patient was advised to engage in a supervised walking program. We will monitor the progression of the atherosclerotic changes and schedule a follow-up in three months.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with intermittent claudication (no HCC in V28): I70.211.

distractors.why: Rest pain is not documented (it would add HCC 264).
Atherosclerosis with claudication is documented: I70.21-.
